title: Agentic Coding as an Engineer
summary: Three mornings (Dec 28–30) on working with coding agents like a professional engineer. Neither the curriculum site nor the syllabus describes this block yet, so the exact topics are unconfirmed. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Work with a coding agent the way an engineer does: plan first, review every change, and stay in control of the code.

steps.title: Review the Prompting Life Cycle
steps.detail: Reread the Phase III Prompt Life Cycle lesson from your first week. The course builds on Define → Explore → Plan → Code → Review → Commit.
steps.doneWhen: You can list the six stages from memory and say what you do in each.

steps.title: Log what went wrong with Claude during your personal project
steps.detail: From Dec 4 to Dec 22 you'll build a lot with Claude Code. Each time it went off track (wrong file, skipped a test, too much code), write one line in your daily notes. That gives you real cases to bring to these mornings.
steps.doneWhen: Your notes list at least 3 real moments with what you'd do differently.

steps.title: Read Anthropic's Claude Code best practices
steps.detail: Pick one practice you haven't tried yet (for example, having Claude write a plan before coding, or using a subagent for review) and try it once.
steps.doneWhen: You've tried one new practice and written a sentence about how it went.

concepts.meaning: Letting an AI agent read files, run commands and make changes while you direct and review.
The course's loop: Define, Explore, Plan, Code, Review, Commit.
How much text the model can keep in mind at once; long sessions push old details out.
A separate agent Claude starts for one focused job, like a review or a search.
